name: Ground support installation
summary: After each development round is blasted and mucked, the rock above and beside the new opening must be held in place before anyone can work under it. A bolter operator examines and scales the heading, then installs screen and rock bolts one hole at a time on a 1.2 m pattern to the face, with extra support such as shotcrete or cable bolts where the geotechnical engineer finds poor ground. The supervisor checks the work and marks the heading ready for the next round. The heading cannot be drilled until this is done, so a busy bolter, a missing consumable or a wait for the engineer holds up development.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-650 tpd narrow-vein underground mine in northern Ontario on 12-hour shifts and 14-on/14-off rotations, with its own mill.
baseline.notes: Mechanised single-boom bolters with resin rebar or friction bolts and welded-wire screen; shotcrete by a shared sprayer unit; one geotechnical engineer on site.

unit_of_work: one heading supported (one round, or one section of rehabilitation)
trigger: A blasted development round has been mucked out, or a heading needs rehabilitation after inspection.
end_state: Support is installed to the ground control standard to the face, inspected and recorded, and the heading is marked ready for drilling.

volume.seasonality: None underground; rehabilitation work rises after seismic events or falls of ground.

evidence.note: One supported heading per development round (110-190 a month) plus about 10-15% rehabilitation work; matches the organisation file entry. Support-before-entry practice per Macassa.

surge.cause: Rehabilitation campaign after a fall of ground, a seismic event or deterioration found by inspection

evidence.note: Author's estimate; records of falls of ground are required under s. 72 but no frequency for the reference mine was found.
10 bolter operators on four crews (organisation file); most of their shift is bolting. Bolting duties per Job Bank.
Handheld bolting in places the bolter cannot reach.
Bolting list, inspections and fall-of-ground records.
Poor-ground inspections and bolt testing; s. 6 and s. 73 duties.
Shotcrete and cable bolting crew.

systems.name: Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Incident, inspection and training records system

resources.name: Development crew (jumbo, bolter and mucking on one heading set)
Underground utility fleet (scissor lifts and light vehicles)

steps.name: Put the mucked heading on the bolting list
steps.description: When the scooptram operator reports the round mucked out, the shift supervisor adds the heading to the bolting list on the line-up board and assigns a bolter operator, ranking it against other headings waiting for support.

evidence.note: The wait includes mucking out the round in mine-mucking-haulage and the shift change; author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for a bolter and inspect it before use
steps.description: The bolter operator takes over the mechanised bolter when it comes free from another heading or the shop, and does the pre-operational check of the boom, bolting head, hydraulics, brakes, lights and fire suppression, recording defects on the card.

error.defect_description: A defect is missed and the bolter breaks down mid-heading.

control.basis: Company pre-operational (circle check) inspection procedure for mobile equipment

evidence.note: Three bolters for all active headings (organisation file); waiting time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Tram the bolter to the heading
steps.description: The operator drives the bolter to the heading with a load of bolts, resin and screen sheets, calling movements on the radio and giving way to haul trucks.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wash down the back and walls
steps.description: The operator hoses down the back, walls and the muck-pile remnants so cracks, slabs and any explosive left in sockets can be seen before anyone works under the new ground.

evidence.note: Common practice before examining a freshly blasted round; author's estimate.

steps.name: Examine the ground and check for misfires
steps.description: From under the last row of support the operator examines the unsupported span for loose rock, open joints and misfired explosive, and fills in the workplace inspection card.

error.defect_description: Loose rock or a geological structure that needs heavier support is missed.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, s. 66: ground examined for dangers before work begins

evidence.note: s. 66 examination before work; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Scale the back, walls and face
steps.description: The operator scales loose rock with the bolter's scaling attachment or a bar, working from supported ground forward, until the span sounds solid.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, s. 67.1: scaling, and no other work that hinders scaling

next.condition: poor ground: wide joints, shear zone or water
a fall of ground has occurred

evidence.note: Scaling is a listed miner duty and s. 67.1 requirement; ground-class shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Geotechnical engineer specifies enhanced support
steps.description: The supervisor calls the geotechnical engineer, who inspects the heading, classifies the ground against the support classes in the ground control standard and writes the extra support needed, such as longer bolts, shotcrete or cable bolts.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, s. 6: ground support design under the direction of a professional engineer

evidence.note: Engineer-directed design (s. 6) and five support classes at a comparable mine (Macassa); one geotechnical engineer on rotation, so waits can reach a day.

steps.name: Set up the bolter and stage consumables
steps.description: The operator positions and jacks the bolter, loads rock bolts, resin cartridges and screen sheets for the pattern on the support standard card, and checks there is enough of each for the round.

next.condition: short of bolts, resin or screen

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Fetch missing consumables from stores
steps.description: The operator or a helper drives to the level bay or the surface warehouse to get the missing bolts, resin or screen, signing for them on a stores issue slip.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Install screen and rock bolts to the pattern
steps.description: The operator drills and installs each bolt through the screen one hole at a time on the 1.2 m dice-five pattern in the back and walls, overlapping screen sheets and carrying support to the face, typically 20-30 bolts for a 3.8 m round.

error.defect_description: Bolts short of pattern, wrong length, or screen overlap missing.

control.basis: Company ground control standard (one hole/one bolt, 1.2 m by 1.2 m pattern, screen to the face) under Ontario Regulation 854, s. 67 written procedures for installing ground support

next.condition: face or shanty back needs handheld bolting

evidence.note: One hole/one bolt on a 1.2 m by 1.2 m dice-five pattern with screen to the face at a comparable Ontario mine (Macassa); bolts per round and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Install handheld bolts where the bolter cannot reach
steps.description: A development miner installs bolts with a jackleg or stoper drill in corners, the face or a cut-out the bolter cannot reach, following the same pattern.

error.defect_description: Handheld bolt installed at the wrong angle or not tensioned.

control.basis: Company ground control standard (one hole/one bolt, 1.2 m by 1.2 m pattern, screen to the face) under Ontario Regulation 854, s. 67 written procedures for installing ground support

evidence.note: Drilling and installing rock bolts is a listed miner duty; share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Spray shotcrete or install cable bolts
steps.description: A services crew brings the shotcrete sprayer and a transmixer to spray a fibre-reinforced lining to the thickness specified, or drills and grouts cable bolts at an intersection, as the support instruction requires.

control.basis: Company ground control standard (one hole/one bolt, 1.2 m by 1.2 m pattern, screen to the face) under Ontario Regulation 854, s. 67 written procedures for installing ground support

evidence.note: Shotcrete in poor ground is named in the organisation file; the sprayer is a shared unit (not in the organisation file). Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Wait for shotcrete to cure before re-entry
steps.description: Nobody works under fresh shotcrete until it reaches the early strength in the mine's procedure, so the heading stays closed for several hours.

control.basis: Company shotcrete re-entry time in the ground control standard

evidence.note: Curing times of 4-12 hours before working under shotcrete are common; author's estimate.

steps.name: Pull-test sample bolts
steps.description: The geotechnical engineer or a trained technician pull-tests a sample of the new bolts with a hydraulic jack, or drills a shotcrete thickness check, and records the loads in the testing log.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, s. 73: torque and pull testing of ground support

evidence.note: s. 73 testing of rock bolts and shotcrete thickness; sampling rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Supervisor inspects the supported heading
steps.description: The supervisor checks the bolts and screen reach the face, the pattern is complete and any enhanced support is in, during the shift examination, and either accepts the heading or has missing bolts installed.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, s. 63(1): supervisor examines every drilling and blasting place each shift

evidence.note: Per-shift examination; deficiency rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the support installed
steps.description: The operator writes the heading, support class, number and type of bolts, screen sheets and any shotcrete on the ground support record and the shift report.

error.defect_description: Bolt counts or class recorded wrongly or not at all.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Tram the bolter out and report consumables
steps.description: The operator trams the bolter to the next heading or the parking bay, refuels if needed and reports bolts and resin used so the level bay can be restocked.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Mark the heading ready for drilling
steps.description: The supervisor marks the heading supported on the line-up board so it is assigned to a development crew and jumbo at the next line-up.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Record a fall of ground
steps.description: When rock has fallen from the back or walls, the supervisor closes the area, records the time, location, size and any damage, and notifies the mine captain and the geotechnical engineer before support work resumes.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854, s. 72: record of uncontrolled falls of ground and rockbursts

evidence.note: Record content per the guideline's summary of s. 72; frequency is the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Poor ground needs engineer's support instruction
exceptions.description: The geotechnical engineer must classify the ground and specify heavier support before bolting continues.

exceptions.name: Shotcrete or cable bolts
exceptions.description: Enhanced support needs the shared sprayer and a curing wait before re-entry.

exceptions.name: Missing consumables
exceptions.description: The bolter runs short of bolts, resin or screen and someone fetches more from stores.

exceptions.name: Deficiency found on inspection or testing
exceptions.description: Missing bolts, screen gaps or failed pull tests send the heading back for re-bolting.

exceptions.name: Fall of ground
exceptions.description: A fall of ground is recorded under s. 72 and the engineer inspects before work resumes.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from round mucked (or rehab requested) to heading marked supported, including mucking wait
benchmarks.population: Narrow-vein Ontario underground mine with mechanised bolting

evidence.note: Mucking 2-5 hours, a shift change and 3-5 hours of bolting; author's estimate.
Stated in the Macassa technical report.

pain_points.description: Three bolters serve all headings, so mucked headings queue for a bolter and the jumbo cannot advance meanwhile.

evidence.note: Resource counts from the organisation file; at about 5 bolter-hours per heading and 160 headings a month the three bolters are about 75% utilised. Queue length is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Poor ground waits for the single geotechnical engineer, who works days on rotation.

evidence.note: Organisation file headcount of one geotechnical engineer.

pain_points.description: Shotcrete needs a shared sprayer and hours of curing before the heading reopens.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Support records are handwritten, so the geotechnical team re-keys bolt counts and support classes into its tracking spreadsheet.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 practice.

sources.title: Workplace examinations by supervisors (guideline on section 63 of Regulation 854)
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (archived copy in the Library and Archives Canada web archive)
sources.supports: Regulation 854 s. 63(1): a supervisor examines every place where drilling and blasting is being carried out at least once each work shift; s. 63(3): every other place where workers work, in person, at least once each work week; the examination is to identify potential or actual hazards and assess general conditions. The guideline page is dated February 2024; the archive returned a June 2024 capture.

sources.title: Ground control in underground mines
sources.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (archived copy in the Library and Archives Canada web archive)
sources.supports: Regulation 854 s. 6: mine design assessing ground stability prepared under the direction of a professional engineer; s. 6.1: workers kept out of unsupported excavations unless an engineer's written report allows it; s. 66: ground conditions examined for hazards before work begins; s. 67: written procedures for installing ground support; s. 67.1: no other work that hinders scaling; s. 72: records of falls of ground and rockbursts; s. 73: torque and pull tests of rock bolts. Page dated December 2023.

sources.title: Macassa Mine NI 43-101 Technical Report (April 2019), exhibit 99.20
sources.publisher: Kirkland Lake Gold Ltd. (filed on SEC EDGAR)
sources.supports: Comparable Ontario underground gold mine: one hole/one bolt policy with no pre-drilling; bolts on a 1.2 m by 1.2 m dice-five pattern; standard support carried to the working face and screen above 3 m; five ground support classes; longhole stopes for ore dipping about 45 degrees or steeper, drilled from a drilling horizon, with blasts started from a drop or inverse raise; mobile fleet of LHDs, jumbos, bolters and trucks (Table 15-6).

sources.title: Job description: Underground production and development miners (NOC 83100), near Thunder Bay (ON)
sources.supports: Miners set up and operate drills to produce a designated pattern of blast holes, load explosives and detonate them, scale loose rock from walls and roof, drill and install rock bolts, extend air and water pipes, operate LHDs and do routine maintenance; usually more than 40 hours a week.

assumptions: The cycle includes the wait for mucking (done in mine-mucking-haulage) because a heading cannot be bolted until it is mucked.
touch_min in crew steps counts one operator; occupied_min shows how long the bolter and crew are tied up.
Bolting pattern and one hole/one bolt policy follow the Macassa technical report as a comparable Ontario mine; the reference mine's ground control standard was not found.
Rehabilitation cases (about 13%) follow the same steps and are started by a geotechnical assessment; the organisation file lists only blasted rounds as a trigger.
A shotcrete sprayer is added as a resource (not in the organisation file).
The organisation file lists bolter-operator, dev-miner and ug-shift-supervisor; this file adds geotech-engineer and ug-services-worker, the input shift_lineup and stores_issue from site-warehouse.
Loaded costs from the organisation file.
